summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (compact reference)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "In the Mayor's Parlour" by J. S. Fletcher (1922, John Lane)

**Setting:** Hathelsborough, fictional old English borough. Market-place with High Cross (east, before Moot Hall) and Low Cross (west, before St. Hathelswide's church). Moot Hall (east end; ex-Mayor's residence next door, old bank on other side). Iron gates, curfew rung from St. Hathelswide's tower, 60 min after sunset. Castle (Norman keep, Castle grounds with bench in angle of walls), Meadow Gate, River Gate, Barley Market, Abbey Gate, Farthing Lane, St. Laurence Lane (back of Moot Hall), Piper's Passage, Copper Alley, Strand Lane, Woolmarket, Little Bailey Gate, Waterdale, Lingmore Cross Roads, Clothford (neighbour city), Marriner's Laundry.

**Characters:**
- John Wallingford: Mayor, murdered; ~41; came to town 12 yrs before as managing clerk; reformer; elected Mayor by one vote (481st Mayor); carried gold chain, furred mantle; grey tweed coat; careless dress.
- Richard Brent: London journalist, Wallingford's cousin, sole heir (~£15,000); tall, clean-shaven, square jaw, grey eyes, brusque. Later buys Acacia Lodge (2,000 guineas, from John Chillingham via Tansley), stands for Castle Ward Council vacancy, loses (about 100 votes). Engaged to Queenie.
- Bunning: caretaker/ex-sergeant-major of Moot Hall; wife (Mrs. Bunning, fetches supper beer from Chancellor Vaults ~7:30–8).
- Spizey (Bellman, Town Crier, Mace-Bearer, ~40 yrs in office, livery); wife Sarah Jane Spizey (huge "Grenadier", washed Moot Hall court floor 6–8).
- Hawthwaite: Superintendent of borough police; big, bearded, heavy, unimaginative.
- Dr. Wellesley: police-surgeon, tall, handsome, Councillor (Riverside Ward), Reform man; former suitor of Mrs. Saumarez. Assistant Dr. Rutherford Carstairs (young Scot). Dr. Barber (second doctor).
- Peppermore: editor-reporter of *Monitor*, spectacles, eyebrows; son/boy assistant Jimmy Pryder (red hair, ~15–16).
- Alderman Simon Crood: tanner, Deputy-Mayor, later Mayor (elected by 2 votes); Tannery House; big, flabby, long churchwarden pipe; Town Trustee. Niece Queenie Crood (dark, olive, lustrous eyes; wants stage/London).
- Mallett: bank manager (Bank House), Town Trustee/Borough Auditor, side-whiskers. Wife Mrs. Mallett (handsome, determined; was "caller" at Wellesley's 7:30–7:45; went to Mayor's Parlour door, heard two voices quarrelling; husband left her; later back in town staying in Waterdale).
- Coppinger: borough treasurer, Town Trustee.
- Krevin Crood: Simon's brother, ex-Town Clerk/Magistrates' Clerk, pensioned £150/yr (actually paid £300), tall, grey suit, cicerone of antiquities; drinks at Bull's Snug.
- Samuel Epplewhite: elderly tradesman, Reform party, produced anonymous typed letter (threat, "Mr. Mayor...").
- Tansley: solicitor, Brent's adviser.
- Seagrave: Coroner, keen-faced old lawyer.
- Meeking: barrister for police.
- Mrs. Anita Saumarez: rich young widow of Captain Roderick Francis Saumarez (RN); Abbey House (Abbey Gate, built from ruins of Benedictine Abbey); companion Mrs. Elstrick; was courted by Wellesley and Wallingford; burned cabinet of letters after Brent fetched them. Cabinet contained letters, woman's glove, ribbon, faded flowers.
- Mrs. Appleyard: Wallingford's landlady.
- Louisa Speck: Mallett's parlour-maid (26), saw Krevin given handkerchief from Mallett's drawer.
- Winifred Wilson: Wellesley's housemaid (20), saw Wellesley on landing 7:45 in white jacket; met Joe Green.
- Mrs. Marriner: laundry proprietor, identified handkerchief as Wellesley's (French cambric).
- Walkershaw: Borough Surveyor (diagrams; private door Wellesley house–Moot Hall, 1 minute).
- Dr. Septimus Pellery: antiquary, revealed secret passage through St. Lawrence tower/connecting arch to Mayor's Parlour (fifth panel left wall; panel slides).
- Samuel Owthwaite: mechanic at Green & Polford (Clothford), identified Simon's Semmingford typewriter (no. 32,587).
- Matthew James Nettleton: Borough Accountant, resigned; testified Town Trustees' falsified books, Krevin's pension secretly £300.
- Mrs. Bunning's absence (~7:30–8) used by Krevin.
- Detective-Sergeant Welton: found in Krevin's lodgings Wallingford's papers (56, some bloodstained); in Simon's Tannery desk 17 papers and red-leather memorandum book.
- Sergeant Pryder (father of Jimmy), Robertshaw (policeman).

**Key objects:** Cambric handkerchief fragment (Wellesley's; burnt/bloodstained); Spanish rapier (bought from curiosity dealer, found behind bookcase; killed Wallingford, wound in back, through heart); red-leather memorandum book (found in Simon's drawer); typed letter (Simon's machine, Semmingford, broken letters, slanted small t); facsimile supplement "WHO TYPED THIS LETTER?" (5,000 copies).

**Chronology:**
- April evening: Wallingford enters Moot Hall ~7:25, tells Bunning to show cousin Brent up. Spizey conversation with Bunning. Brent arrives, finds Wallingford dead ~8 pm, curfew ringing.
- Next: Hawthwaite, dock stair, handkerchief found; Brent to Crood (Tannery, Barley Market; Queenie's request to meet at Castle).
- Day 2: Brent at Bull's Snug; Krevin remark; Hawthwaite shows rapier; wills found (executed a week before); inquest opens day 2; Mrs. Saumarez summoned; Epplewhite's letter; adjournment 10 days.
- Mrs. Saumarez summons; cabinet burnt. Town Clerk visit re public funeral; Brent buys Acacia Lodge; election poster; Mayor election (Crood by 2 votes).
- Adjourned inquest: Carstairs (19-minute absence 7:30–7:49), Wellesley, Mrs. Marriner, Winifred Wilson, Mrs. Mallett intervenes; Mrs. Bunning; Krevin's St. Lawrence Lane theory; adjourned one month.
- Special edition with facsimile; Queenie's note; Brent kisses Queenie at Castle wall; Simon catches them.
- Brent loses Castle Ward election (~100 votes); articles in Monitor; LGB inspector; Krevin & Simon arrested; Mallett & Coppinger absconded; Owthwaite, Nettleton, Louisa Speck, Pellery, Spizey, Welton testify; Krevin confesses: Mayor killed by Mrs. Saumarez (who was in room with Wallingford, quarrelling over letters; she struck with rapier). Mrs. Elstrick fled in motor. Mrs. Saumarez gone (telegram "Lingmore Cross Roads six-thirty" from Mallett). Brent last scene: Queenie shelling peas in garden. END.

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: "The Spring Song" by Forrest Reid (1916, Edward Arnold)

**Characters:**
- Griffith "Grif" Weston: 13, sensitive, sleepy-gentle eyes (like Perugino angels), sleepwalker, hears flute / Spring Song; delicate health (fevers, colds). Pet bulldog Pouncer (also called "Bouncer" by Ann).
- Siblings: Barbara (12, prim, white muslin), Ann (10, fat, freckled, reddish hair; calls Palmer "Balmer"; Edward "Angelina" nickname), Jim (9, scout, riddles, white sailor suit).
- Edward Weston (15, fair, blue eyes, pointed chin, smokes, vain about clothes, plays cricket, school friend of Palmer).
- Palmer Dorset (15-ish, short, sturdy, bright red crisp hair, freckles, reddish-brown small eyes, Sherlock Holmes-style detective, revolver, life-preserver from grandpapa's room; invented games; shoots burglar George).
- Miss Johnson: governess, pince-nez, writing novel *Be True, Fond Heart* (Reginald, Angelina, Maud Vivien, Captain Victor De Lancy).
- Aunt Caroline (Miss Annesley): tall, fair, smiling; father's housekeeper/manager; writes letters to her sister.
- Canon Annesley (grandpapa): thin, bent, bald, black velvet cap, writing book on fairies (*The Golden Bough* on desk), organ rope; college friend of Bradley.
- Mr. Drummond: curate, youthful, smooth-faced, disapproving.
- Mr. Clement Bradley: organist, wild silver hair, black suit, ebony gold-headed stick, sly cat-like eyes, real name Tennant; killed a man (his brother/father figure) on a bridge after shadow obsession; asylum; sings Spring Song; claimed ghost of boy Billy.
- Billy (William Batt Tremaine), grandson of Captain Batt, died aged 14 about four years earlier; grave in churchyard; flute; was to play Spring Song at village concert.
- Captain Narcissus Batt, Miss Nancy Batt (kind, kisses Grif), Miss Jane Batt (very old, frail voice). Red brick house, cedar tree, pond with water-lilies. Miss Nancy gives Grif comfort.
- Doctor O'Neill: physician, bachelor 30–35, ugly-fine face, car; befriends Palmer; gives him revolver; visits Bradley with Palmer.
- Pan and Syrinx: stable cats. Bridget and Hannah: servants. Johnnie: boy who cleans knives/boots (bitten by Pouncer, Daniel-and-lion game).
- Robert: coachman.
- Circus: Prairie Dick (rider), George (earring man, stole Pouncer; shot in leg by Palmer), a woman with stick, half-dressed boy in tree.

**Places:** Glebe house (Canon's), wood behind wall, river (irises, purple), Batts' red-brick house, Ballinreagh (town/station), Rathcarragh (circus), St. Laurence? (no—church at Glebe village, yew path, rose window), croquet-lawn, cedar, ash-tree "Jonah's Bower", tool-shed, Billy's room, Miss Johnson's room.

**Events in order:**
1. June train to grandpapa's; Pouncer; Aunt Caroline meets at station; walk; Grif asks for room near wood (chooses window over wood, swallow nest); meets Mr. Bradley in lane (silver hair, sly eyes).
2. Edward and Palmer arrive; Jim's riddle "bun"; Edward called "Angelina" at school; Palmer's red hair; cigarettes; dinner; Miss Johnson's novel; Jim's croquet challenge with grandpapa vs Edward/Palmer.
3. Night: Grif at window hears voices of wood; sings; hears flute; Pouncer on bed.
4. Morning tournament drawn; Grif meets Captain Batt (Narcissus) & sisters by garden door; gooseberries; cat; tea; lunch; learns of Billy Tremaine.
5. Grif at church hears Bradley play; sings for him; Bradley says ghost (Billy) appeared.
6. Grif late home; Miss Johnson's complaints.
7. Rain; Miss Johnson bathing scene (naked boy at river); Jim bitten by Pouncer; Palmer's devil talk; play *Be True Fond Heart* performed (Reginald, Angelina/Ann, Maud, Mr. Drummond's hat sat upon; bottle breaks; liquorice wine).
8. Circus; Pouncer stolen by George; Grif runs after circus by train, walks, sleeps by stream; night rescue of Pouncer among circus dogs; sleeps near house.
9. Edward & Palmer's night watch; George caught at wall; Palmer shoots him in leg; canon interrogates; Doctor O'Neill called; Palmer's revolver returned.
10. Grif wakes in sun; eats at Batts'-type house (actually lunch elsewhere); visits church; Bradley's flute by river; Grif sings Spring Song.
11. Grif back home; Palmer suspicious; Bradley warns/hypnotizes; Grif sleepwalks, fainting; Bradley visits Grif (shadow story); Grif ill three days.
12. Doctor O'Neill & Palmer visit Bradley's lodgings; Palmer finds real name Tennant; Bradley rude; Palmer's shadow remark; Bradley's face shows malice.
13. Miss Johnson's birthday (34 by Palmer's trick); fireworks; bonfire stopped.
14. Church fire; Bradley on tower leaps to death; Doctor O'Neill; canon.
15. Aftermath: Bradley's history revealed; Grif's decline; Aunt Caroline plans school; doctor insists no school; Grif visits Miss Nancy, Billy's room, realizes "it is all different"; falls asleep in Miss Nancy's arms. END.

**Notable quoted lines:** "Be kind to Victor"; "Look not for whales in the Euxine sea" (canon); "Petit chaudron, grandes oreilles" (Aunt Caroline); Spring Song verses ("Who is this human boy").
